title: Dependency Visibility Broker and Hotpath Triage for Cross-Team Roadmaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We lack a lightweight, machine-assisted way to detect and triage 'hotpath' roadmap dependencies across Engineering, Design, Security, and Infra. Current dependency lists are overly manual, stale between planning cycles, and do not prioritize which dependencies are on critical execution paths.

Proposal: Build a Dependency Visibility Broker (DVB) — a thin service that ingests signals from Linear, GitHub PRs, Console rollout config, design handoff docs, and security review requests to compute a running 'hotpath' ranking and expose triage workflows. DVB will: 1) surface prioritized dependency cards for PMs and ICs, 2) compute confidence and risk scores using simple heuristics (ownership absence, cross-team overlap, release window proximity), 3) power a triage lane in the roadmap dashboard with recommended mitigations (escalate, re-scope, fallback model), and 4) provide an API to integrate with the Console rollout and the Incident Escalation playbook.

Scope: MVP focuses on read-side synthesis for PMs: aggregated signals, UX in roadmap dashboard, and email/Slack digest. Later phases add autosnooze rules, simulation (what-if cutover windows), and automatic runbooks.

Out-of-scope: Full automation of capacity allocation, enforcement of ownership, and replacing human judgment.

Trade-offs considered: keep initial scoring explainable (no heavy ML) to win trust; accept some false positives to avoid missed hotpaths; prioritize integration breadth over depth in MVP.
acceptance_criteria: DVB ingests at least three distinct signals: Linear blocking links, GitHub open PRs touching serving/runtime, and Console rollout schedules
Roadmap dashboard shows a top-10 hotpath dependency feed filtered by product area and release window
Each dependency card displays computed risk score and three suggested mitigations with links to source artifacts
PM/Eng/design reviewers can mark a dependency as triaged, escalate to security, or link to an existing incident/PR
Weekly digest to #pm-roadmap and a pager-adjacent channel is configured and contains actionable items
Telemetry: at least one signal contributing to score is recorded for 95% of surfaced cards (no opaque scores)
comments: 2025-11-05 - Sync: Kickoff with Eng (Luca, Mei), Design (Rohit), and Security (Priya). Agreed MVP signals and explained desire for explainable heuristic scoring.
2025-11-06 - PM note: Draft PRD uploaded: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/DVB-MVP. Designers requested a compact card with clear CTAs (triage/escalate/link).

2025-11-10 - Engineering input: Backend will expose a /v1/dependencies endpoint; plan to reuse existing Linear webhooks and Console schedule API. Trade-off: prefer eventual consistency to avoid blocking API pressure.
2025-11-12 - Design review: Figma mockups available: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/DVB-cards. Recommended color coding for risk levels and an explicit confidence tooltip.
2025-11-14 - Security review sync: Security asks for an opt-in flag for listing security-sensitive dependencies and a manual escalation button. Will capture as non-blocking MVP item.

2025-11-16 - Decision: Use deterministic heuristics for MVP: ownership missing (+30), cross-team crossing (+20), release within 2 weeks (+25), open PRs touching runtime (+15). Scores normalized to 0-100 with explanation strings stored.
2025-11-18 - Next steps: Eng to spin up DVB proto service (ENG-19852), PM to prioritize dashboard placement (PM-31416 as parent), Design to finalize microcopy and CTAs.
